children: Japan’s Kobelco Construction Machinery’s $1-billion acquisition of a majority stake in Netherlands-based CNH Industrial’s construction-equipment business could create a stronger challenger in India’s earthmoving machinery market, combining Kobelco’s Sri City excavator plant with CASE’s Pithampur facility, complementary product portfolios and international distribution networks at a time when domestic sales are weakening and exports are expanding.

Announced on November 9, 2026, the transaction could reshape competition through greater manufacturing scale, a wider equipment range, enhanced export opportunities, technology adoption and increased competitive pressure on established players.

Kobelco will hold 70 per cent of the new venture, with CNH retaining 30 per cent. CNH expects $700 million in cash, subject to adjustments, to reduce debt. Its Indian construction-equipment subsidiary will transfer to the venture after the global transaction closes.

Humayun Chishti, CNH’s Construction Segment President and expected Chief Executive of the venture, described Kobelco as “the ideal partner, a global excavator and crane specialist with leading technology”.
Two factories, one opportunity
CASE’s Pithampur facility in Madhya Pradesh manufactures backhoe loaders, compactors and crawler excavators, while Kobelco’s Sri City plant in Andhra Pradesh specialises in hydraulic excavators.

“The significance of this transaction for India lies in the complementary manufacturing and product capabilities of the two companies. The opportunity will be to improve localisation, optimise costs and strengthen distribution without disrupting existing operations,” said Aveek Chattopadhyay, an automotive industry analyst.
India’s construction-equipment sales declined 2.3 per cent to 1,36,995 units in FY26 from 1,40,191 in FY25. Domestic sales fell 6.7 per cent, while exports rose 32 per cent.
Earthmoving remained the largest category at 97,236 units, down 2 per cent. Material-handling equipment declined 10 per cent, while road-construction machinery grew 6.3 per cent.

In FY25, India sold 53,133 backhoe loaders and 35,816 crawler excavators, categories where CASE and Kobelco have complementary capabilities. FADA’s wheeled-equipment registrations rose 1.6 per cent to 34,637 in H1 FY27 and 22 per cent to 7,434 in October. These figures exclude tracked excavators.
Exports and global scale

“The construction-equipment industry is seeing a divergence between domestic demand and exports. While infrastructure spending provides long-term opportunities, project execution determines near-term purchases. A larger global platform could help balance domestic fluctuations with overseas demand,” said Kranthi Bathini, Director, Equity Strategy, WealthMills Securities.

CNH’s international construction-equipment network and Kobelco’s global presence could widen export opportunities for Indian manufacturing operations, although no additional export mandates have been announced.
CNH’s agriculture dealers will continue to access construction equipment through the venture, while CNH Capital will support customers and dealers with financing and related services.
Technology meets competition
Kobelco brings hydraulic-excavator engineering and K-DIVE remote-operation technology, while CNH contributes compact machinery platforms and electric-equipment development capabilities.
Together, these capabilities could support advances in fuel efficiency, machine connectivity and alternative powertrains. No India-specific technology programme has been announced.
A wider portfolio could increase competitive pressure on JCB, Tata Hitachi, Komatsu and SANY, although market share gains will depend on pricing, distribution and after-sales support.
Kobelco’s India test
For CNH, the transaction advances its shift towards agricultural equipment and precision technology, with New Holland’s tractor operations remaining outside the venture.

For Kobelco, the challenge will be translating majority ownership into a stronger Indian business. Kobelco India is led by Managing Director Jun Hayama, while Chishti is expected to head the global venture.
Whether Kobelco can translate the deal into manufacturing efficiencies, stronger exports and wider market reach will determine its impact on India’s construction-equipment industry.

title: Kobelco’s $1 billion CNH deal could redraw India’s construction equipment landscape
